title: Deleting a customer type in Saleor's API, built by its owner for a requester whose replies come 60 minutes late (a slice of the August 2026 customer attributes feature)

exact: `saleor/graphql/schema.graphql` is the public API contract and is as it is today, without the mutation. Bring it up to date from the code (`python manage.py get_graphql_schema > saleor/graphql/schema.graphql`): the schema the code generates must equal it. What the work adds to the API is listed above, under "The API the tests call".
`PluginsManager.customer_type_deleted(customer_type, webhooks=None)` exists already; the mutation calls it once the type is deleted, and the tests patch it.
The error type's codes are `saleor.account.error_codes.CustomerTypeDeleteErrorCode`, which exists already; deleting the default type gives `CANNOT_DELETE_DEFAULT` on field `id`.

overview:
The company runs the Saleor commerce platform as two systems, each a repository of its own:
- `core` (Python, Django): the commerce API, in GraphQL. It has the only database.
- `dashboard` (TypeScript, React): the application staff use. It keeps no data: every screen calls core's API. It holds copies of core's GraphQL schema and generates its typed query code from them, so the copies must match the API core really serves.
Each system runs in a container of its own. The containers can reach each other by system name: the API a core container serves on port 8000 is at `http://core:8000/graphql/` from the dashboard's container.

notes.core: - To serve the API to the other containers of this work: `python manage.py migrate` (two minutes), then `nohup python manage.py runserver 0.0.0.0:8000 > /tmp/server.log 2>&1 &`. It takes about half a minute to answer, at `http://core:8000/graphql/`. `python manage.py populatedb --createsuperuser` adds sample data and a staff user (`admin@example.com` / `admin`).
notes.dashboard: - The containers of this work can reach each other by name: once somebody serves core's API from the container of a `core` checkout they may push from, it is at `http://core:8000/graphql/`.

feature: We would like one thing added to the API. This is what it should do.

core.where: the API, at `http://core:8000/graphql/`, with sample data and a staff user (`admin@example.com` / `admin`). A deploy runs its database migrations.

dashboard.where: the staff application, served by its development server at `http://dashboard:9000/`, calling the API above.

description:
Customers are grouped into customer types, the way products are grouped into product types. A customer type has a name and the set of attributes its customers share, and exactly one type is the default. Staff who hold the permission for it can already create and rename types, make a type the default, and assign, reorder and unassign a type's attributes.

**Deleting a customer type.** What is missing is deleting one: a `customerTypeDelete` mutation, beside `customerTypeCreate` and `customerTypeUpdate` and for the same permission. The default type cannot be deleted, even if it only becomes the default while the deletion is under way. Apps are told of a deletion through the `CUSTOMER_TYPE_DELETED` webhook event, which exists already.
done: It is done when it is on `main` of `core` and works there: the API starts on a fresh database, and the tests the repository has today still pass. `INTERFACE.md` lists the names the project's own tests for this mutation use; keep to them.
source: Real changes to Saleor (BSD-3-Clause), August 2026; the start is authored by taking Saleor's delete mutation out of the merged feature
